metadata.name: trajectory-power-phase5-design-point-pilot
metadata.intent: Phase 5 design-point pilot (readiness item 4): measure how orientation's operating characteristics scale with samples per group-stage cell and baseline continuity, on an uncensored effect axis, so the paper-grade design point is chosen on evidence. Modes are orientation (the estimand whose power floor is in question) and translation (the location-only negative control that binds the surgery headroom). Crossed design grid rho in {0.0, 0.5, 0.8} x n_samples in {300, 600, 1200}; pooled PLS on M-value methylation, four stages, p_dmp = 0.1, 100 replicates, 199 permutations, matched seeds with one shared zero-effect anchor per design point.
notes: p_dmp is 0.1 rather than the Phase 4 pilot's 0.2 so the 0.25-1.00 effect axis is realizable without censoring for every pool-limited mode at every design point, including the rho = 0 stress-test endpoint (orientation saturates near e = 1.69 and translation near e = 2.00 at rho = 0; both grow with rho). Changing p_dmp is a baseline change that touches every mode; magnitude and shape are deliberately left out of this pilot to halve its compute (they reached power 1.00 at n = 300 in Phase 4 and only gain from larger n), and are re-measured at the chosen design point in the Phase 5 study itself.

surgery_censoring is left at its default ('error'): a surgery that cannot be realized in full fails loudly, and enumeration rejects over-headroom cells before compute is spent. Do not copy the historical 'clamp' flag from the Phase 4 configs.

Design-point cells share the primary matched-seed family. rho = 0 and rho > 0 threshold the same uniform block, so comparisons along rho at fixed n are paired at the baseline indicator draw; columns that differ in n_samples simply diverge. Each non-baseline design point owns its own zero-effect anchor, so every column has its own null measurement.

The design-point decision rule is advisory and predeclared: the chosen point is the first column in (n_samples ascending, then rho ascending) order whose orientation/angle power at the top effect clears 0.80 with a one-SE lower-bound confirmation; if none does, the verdict is revise_claim and the readiness worklist revises the claim, not the Monte Carlo size. Lower n is cheaper for Phase 5 and for any real cohort; lower rho is the more general claim.

Power is read beside the recorded pooled configuration eigengap and the angle null-width dispersion (design_point_operating.csv, continuity_resolved_orientation.csv), because the eigengap - not the knob - is the observable that carries a continuity-conditioned orientation claim to real data.

The Phase 4 gate is disabled: this pilot chooses a design point, it does not gate Phase 5. Attribution diagnostics are off; they answer a different question. Selected PLS dimensionality is recorded but not varied (readiness item 3).

Do not pass --n-jobs: the worker count enters the parameter signature and changes the realized permutation draws. Parallelize across shards. Expect roughly 6,500 work units; PLS double CV scales about linearly in n_samples, so the n = 1200 columns dominate compute.
